To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diagnostic accuracy of non-invasive tests to predict hepatic steatosis, fibrosis and cirrhosis in patients with NAFLD is not high enough for them to be used in the clinical practice or research.

in a cohort of non-alcoholic fatty disease patients, the presence of advanced fibrosis is associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events and mortality, and that the presence of advanced hepatic fibrosis is associated to the presence of metabolic syndrome.

in NAFLD patients with normal ALT values the non-invasive tests have a poor diagnostic performance for predicting hepatic fibrosis, while the combination of APRI with either FIB-4 or AST-to-platelet ratio index improves diagnostic performance for detecting advanced fibrosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of noninvasive, simple, low cost and reproducible methods that allow the identification of patients at risk of developing diabetes, cardiovascular disease or other diseases associated with obesity.
the development of noninvasive methods to predict the presence of NAFLD and its progression to cirrhosis.
the development and application of new non-invasive tests that allow to assess the severity of the disease in a simple and reproducible way.
